'''Kumble R. Subbaswamy''' is an Indian [[physicist]] and college administrator who served as the 11th [[Chancellor (education)|chancellor]] of the [[University of Massachusetts Amherst]].<ref name="Subbaswamy UMass Amherst">{{cite web|title=Biography of Chancellor Subbaswamy|url=https://www.umass.edu/chancellor/biography-chancellor-subbaswamy|publisher=[[University of Massachusetts Amherst]]|access-date=1 November 2016}}</ref><ref name="Subbaswamy UMass Amherst Inaugration">{{cite web|title=UMass Amherst Inaugurates Kumble Subbaswamy as Chancellor |work=Office of News & Media Relations &#124; UMass Amherst |url=https://www.umass.edu/newsoffice/article/umass-amherst-inaugurates-kumble-subbaswamy-chancellor |publisher=[[University of Massachusetts Amherst]] |access-date=1 November 2016 |url-status=bot: unknown |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161031221844/https://www.umass.edu/newsoffice/article/umass-amherst-inaugurates-kumble-subbaswamy-chancellor |archive-date=31 October 2016 }}</ref> He then served as Interim Senior Vice President for Academic and Student Affairs and Equity until the end of 2024, serving the five-campus [[University of Massachusetts|University of Massachusetts system]].<ref name="Subbaswamy Appt UMass System">{{cite web|title=Outgoing UMass Amherst Chancellor Kumble Subbaswamy Named Interim Senior Vice President for Academic and Student Affairs and Equity|url=https://www.umass.edu/news/article/outgoing-umass-amherst-chancellor-kumble-subbaswamy-named-interim-senior-vice|publisher=[[University of Massachusetts]]|access-date=11 March 2023}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-11-20 |title=Dr. Nefertiti Walker Appointed Senior Vice President for Academic Affairs, Student Affairs, and Equity at UMass {{!}} UMass System |url=https://www.massachusetts.edu/news/dr-nefertiti-walker-appointed-senior-vice-president-academic-student-affairs-umass |access-date=2026-08-16 |website=www.massachusetts.edu |language=en}}</ref> He formerly served as the [[Provost (education)|provost]] of [[University of Kentucky]].

He is a member of the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]]<ref name="Subbaswamy Arts and Sciences">{{cite web|title=Kumble Subbaswamy Elected To American Academy Of Arts & Sciences|date=3 May 2021|url=https://businesswest.com/blog/kumble-subbaswamy-elected-to-american-academy-of-arts-sciences/|publisher=businesswest.com|access-date=5 December 2021}}</ref><ref name="Subbaswamy Arts and Sciences2">{{cite web|title=Kumble R. Subbaswamy has been elected as a new member of the American Academy of Arts & Sciences|url=https://www.umass.edu/news/article/umass-amherst-chancellor-kumble-0|publisher=[[University of Massachusetts Amherst]]|access-date=5 December 2021}}</ref> and also an elected fellow of the [[American Physical Society]], and has research interests in computational chemistry and condensed matter physics.

On June 2, 2022, Subbaswamy announced that he would retire from being the chancellor by the end of June 2023.<ref>{{cite web|title=Umass Amherst chancellor Kumble Subbaswamy announces plans to retire at the end of June 2023|url=https://www.umass.edu/news/article/umass-amherst-chancellor-kumble-subbaswamy-announces-plans-retire-end-june-2023|publisher=[[University of Massachusetts Amherst]]|access-date=2 June 2022}}</ref>

==Early life and education==
Subbaswamy was born in the city of [[Bangalore]], [[Karnataka]] in [[India]]. He earned a [[Bachelor of Science]] degree in physics from [[Bangalore University]], a [[Master of Science]] in physics from [[University of Delhi]],<ref>{{cite web | url=http://alumni.du.ac.in/archive/pdfs/picture/9.pdf | title=Dr Kumble R Subbaswamy named Chancellor of UMass Amherst | publisher=University of Delhi | access-date=24 October 2018 }}{{Dead link|date=July 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref> and a [[Doctor of Philosophy]] in physics from [[Indiana University Bloomington]].

==Career==
===Academia===
He served as [[research associate]] in the department of physics at the [[University of California, Irvine]] from 1976 to 1978.<ref name="Subbaswamy CV UMass Amherst">{{cite web|title=Official Curriculum Vitae of Chancellor Subbaswamy|url=https://www.umass.edu/chancellor/sites/default/files/cv.pdf|publisher=[[University of Massachusetts Amherst]]|access-date=1 November 2016}}</ref> He later joined as [[assistant professor]] at [[University of Kentucky]] in 1978 and rose to become the chair of the Department of Physics and Astronomy from 1993 to 1997.<ref name="Subbaswamy CV UMass Amherst"/>

He also served as [[adjunct professor]] (Professore a contratto) at [[University of Pavia]] in [[Italy]] in 1990.<ref name="Subbaswamy CV UMass Amherst"/>

He later served as the [[Dean (education)|dean]] of the College of Arts and Sciences in the  Department of Physics at both [[University of Miami]] and [[Indiana University Bloomington]].<ref name="Subbaswamy CV UMass Amherst"/> He then served as the [[Provost (education)|provost]] of [[University of Kentucky]].<ref name="Subbaswamy CV UMass Amherst"/>

After becoming chancellor of the University of Massachusetts Amherst in 2012, he and his wife worked with the UMass Permaculture Committee<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://scholarworks.umass.edu/permaculture/|title=UMass Amherst Permaculture Initiative {{!}} University of Massachusetts - Amherst Research {{!}} ScholarWorks@UMass Amherst|website=scholarworks.umass.edu|access-date=2019-12-05}}</ref> to create a sustainable garden featuring [[Southeast Asia]]n plants at their Hillside residence on [[campus]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.localumass.com/hillside.html|title=Hillside|website=Sustainability|language=en|access-date=2019-12-05}}</ref>

After retiring as UMass Amherst chancellor, he was appointed  senior vice president for academic and student affairs and equity, serving the UMass five-campus, 74,000-student system.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nhpr.org/2023-06-30/kumble-subbaswamy-says-goodbye-to-umass-amherst-while-javier-reyes-says-hello|title=goodbye|website=nhpr|language=en|access-date=2023-06-30}}</ref>

==Honors and awards==
He was awarded an honorary [[Doctor of Humane Letters]]<ref>{{cite web |url=https://honorsandawards.iu.edu/awards/honoree/3895.html |title=University Honors & Awards |publisher=[[Indiana University Bloomington]] |date= |access-date=February 3, 2023 |url-status= |archive-url= |archive-date=}}</ref> from [[Indiana University Bloomington]] during 2019 Winter Commencement. He was also awarded Chancellor and Provost Medallion in 2006 and also IU Foundation President's Medallion from [[Indiana University Bloomington]].

==Selected publications==
* Local Density Theory of Polarizability (Physics of Solids and Liquids) (Publisher: Springer, Publication Year: 1st ed. 1990 edition (31 December 2013); {{ISBN|978-1489924889}}).
